mainTopic: The טבריא hot-water incident, what kind of washing the משנה forbids, and the ruling like רבי יהודה
overview: The people of טבריא ran a pipe of cold water through the hot springs so it would be hot on שבת. The רבנן forbade it, so the גמרא learns that הטמנה in something that adds heat is forbidden, even if it is set up before שבת. עולא wants to rule like the people of טבריא, but רב נחמן answers that they themselves broke their pipes. The גמרא then asks what kind of רחיצה the משנה forbids. Whole-body bathing clashes with a ברייתא, and face-hands-feet would make the סיפא follow בית שמאי. רב איקא בר חנניא answers that the משנה means rinsing the whole body, following רבי שמעון against רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רב חסדא's statement about water in a כלי versus water in the ground is corrected because of the טבריא incident. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה. רב יוסף asks whether this ruling was explicit or inferred from the rule that the הלכה follows the מכריע, a rule with an exception for מטלניות whose reasons continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The טבריא incident teaches that heat-adding insulation is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: From the fact that the רבנן forbade the people of טבריא their pipe-heated water, we learn that הטמנה in something that adds heat is forbidden, even before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what the people of טבריא did, and the fact that the רבנן forbade it to them, we learn that הטמנה in something that adds heat was abolished. This applies even when it is done while it is still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a practical rule out of the story of the people of טבריא and their cold-water pipe running through the hot springs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Running a cold-water pipe through hot springs works like wrapping a pot in something that keeps adding heat. The רבנן forbade the result, so the גמרא concludes that this type of הטמנה is forbidden. The surprising part is that it is forbidden even if it is set up before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: an incident or event that teaches a law
the people of the city of Tiberias
insulating or wrapping a pot to keep it hot
while it is still day, before שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is only about doing הטמנה on שבת itself. The point here is that it is forbidden even if done before שבת begins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a basic source for the rule that one may not insulate food in a heat-adding material, even on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: From the incident that the people of Tiberias did
and the Rabbis forbade it to them
insulating was abolished
in something that adds heat,
and even while it is still day (before Shabbat).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא וְאָסְרִי לְהוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the earlier discussion of the Tiberias pipe by drawing a practical law from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הטמנה in a heat-adding material is forbidden, even if done before שבת.

steps.title: עולא rules like the people of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the הלכה follows the people of טבריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The הלכה is like the people of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא disagrees with the conclusion above and says we should follow the practice of the people of טבריא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's position is that heating water by running a pipe through hot springs is permitted. This goes against the idea that the רבנן abolished such heating.

keyTerms.meaning: the law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The halakha is in accordance with the people of Tiberias.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a ruling that goes against the conclusion of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The practice of the people of טבריא is permitted.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the people of טבריא already broke their pipes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects עולא's ruling by pointing out that the people of טבריא themselves abandoned the practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: The people of טבריא already broke their pipes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on עולא and shows that even the people of טבריא stopped doing this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people of טבריא broke their own pipes, they accepted the רבנן's ban. So there is no one left to rule like, and עולא's ruling is rejected.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
The people of Tiberias have already broken their pipes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: כְּבָר תַּבְרִינְהוּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: עולא's ruling to follow the people of טבריא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The people of טבריא themselves abandoned the practice, so there is no opinion left to follow.
steps.whatToRemember: The ban on the טבריא heating method stands. Even the people of טבריא broke their pipes.

steps.title: What kind of washing does the משנה forbid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about the people of טבריא and asks what kind of רחיצה is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the incident of the people of טבריא in the משנה: what kind of רחיצה is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion on the wording of the משנה. It is setting up a search for the meaning of the word רחיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that, on שבת, the Tiberias water is like water heated on שבת and forbidden for רחיצה. The גמרא wants to know whether that means the whole body or only part of it.

phrases.english: The incident that the people of Tiberias did:
What is meant by 'bathing'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָשׂוּ אַנְשֵׁי טְבֶרְיָא: מַאי רְחִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רחיצה in the משנה mean washing the whole body or only part of it?

steps.title: Whole-body bathing does not fit the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: If רחיצה means the whole body, the משנה implies that water heated before שבת is fine for this. But a ברייתא forbids whole-body washing even with such water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose you say it means washing the whole body. Then only water heated on שבת would be forbidden, and water heated on ערב שבת would be permitted. But a ברייתא teaches that with water heated on ערב שבת, one may wash his face, hands and feet the next day, but not his whole body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning, the whole body, and shows that it clashes with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה singles out water heated on שבת, which implies that water heated before שבת is permitted for the same use. But the ברייתא forbids whole-body washing even with water heated before שבת. So the משנה cannot be talking about the whole body.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is built on an implication. The משנה only says water heated on שבת is forbidden, so the גמרא infers that water heated before שבת must be allowed for the same washing.

phrases.english: If you say it means washing his entire body —

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת הוּא דַּאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: then it is only water heated on Shabbat that is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: הָא חַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת מוּתָּרִין?
phrases.english: but water heated on Shabbat eve is permitted?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
Hot water heated on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: לְמָחָר רוֹחֵץ בָּהֶן פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו,
phrases.english: the next day one may wash with it his face, hands and feet,
but not his entire body!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רחיצה as whole-body washing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading implies water heated before שבת is permitted for the whole body, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: So it means face, hands and feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה must mean washing the face, hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means washing his face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the second possible meaning: washing only the face, hands and feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Per the ברייתא, these limbs may be washed with water heated before שבת. So the משנה's implication now works: only water heated on שבת is forbidden for them.

phrases.english: Rather, it means his face, hands and feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 in light of the problem raised in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רחיצה in the משנה means washing the face, hands and feet.

steps.title: Quoting the סיפא about יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the latter clause of the משנה: on יום טוב, the water is forbidden for רחיצה but permitted for drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the latter clause: On יום טוב, it is like water heated on יום טוב. It is forbidden for רחיצה and permitted for drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה. This is a setup for a new problem with the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רחיצה means face, hands and feet, then the סיפא forbids even washing the feet with water heated on יום טוב. The next step shows why that is a problem.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כְּחַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: On a Festival, it is like water heated on a Festival,
and it is forbidden for bathing and permitted for drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a challenge to the answer in step 6.

steps.title: The משנה would follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: If even foot-washing is forbidden on יום טוב, the unattributed משנה matches בית שמאי, who forbid heating water for one's feet, against בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that we learned an unattributed משנה like בית שמאי? For we learned: בית שמאי say a person may not heat water for his feet unless it is also fit for drinking, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the face-hands-feet reading because it would make the משנה follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל allow heating water on יום טוב to wash one's feet. So forbidding foot-washing fits only בית שמאי. An unattributed משנה (סתם משנה) normally follows the accepted הלכה, which is בית הלל, so this reading is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of Hillel, whose view is usually the הלכה

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned an unattributed mishna like Beit Shammai?
As we learned, Beit Shammai say:
A person may not heat water for his feet
unless it is fit for drinking,
and Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רחיצה as face, hands and feet (step 6)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the סיפא forbid foot-washing on יום טוב, which only בית שמאי hold, but a סתם משנה should not follow בית שמאי.

steps.title: רב איקא בר חנניא: the משנה means rinsing the whole body
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בר חנניא answers that the משנה is talking about rinsing (not bathing) the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא בר חנניא said: We are dealing with rinsing the whole body with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא בר חנניא offers a third meaning of רחיצה that avoids both earlier problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rinsing (pouring water over oneself) is a lighter act than full bathing. Water heated for the whole body is forbidden on יום טוב even according to בית הלל, so the סיפא no longer has to follow בית שמאי. The ברייתא's ban on the whole body can be understood as bathing, not rinsing.
steps.confusionAlert: Rinsing (שטיפה) is not the same as bathing (רחיצה). The ברייתא forbade bathing the whole body. Rinsing is a separate question.

phrases.english: Rav Ika bar Chananya said:
We are dealing with rinsing one's entire body with it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר חֲנַנְיָא: לְהִשְׁתַּטֵּף בָּהֶן כׇּל גּוּפוֹ עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenges of steps 5 and 8 with a new reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: rinsing instead of bathing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רחיצה meant either full-body bathing or washing the face, hands and feet.
steps.terutzMaskana: רחיצה here means rinsing the whole body.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון on rinsing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the תנא behind the משנה: רבי שמעון, who permits rinsing the whole body with water heated before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the opinion of the תנא of the ברייתא: A person may not rinse his whole body, whether with hot water or cold. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי שמעון permits it. רבי יהודה says: with hot water it is forbidden, with cold water it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which תנא agrees with the new reading of the משנה. That is רבי שמעון, who allows rinsing with water heated before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that rinsing is forbidden only with water heated on שבת, and permitted with water heated before. רבי מאיר forbids rinsing completely, and רבי יהודה forbids it with any hot water. Only רבי שמעון fits, permitting rinsing with water heated before שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the משנה forbids rinsing the whole body with water heated on שבת. It follows רבי שמעון, who permits rinsing with water heated before שבת.

phrases.english: And it is this tanna, as was taught:
A person may not rinse his entire body
whether with hot water or with cold water —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon permits it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
With hot water it is forbidden; with cold water it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב איקא בר חנניא's answer by naming the תנא whose view it matches.
steps.raayaObject: רב איקא בר חנניא's reading that the משנה is about rinsing the whole body
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the dispute of רבי מאיר, רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה about rinsing

steps.title: רב חסדא: The dispute is only about water in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the argument about washing with water heated before שבת applies only to water in a כלי. Water collected in the ground is permitted by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The argument is about water in a vessel. But water in the ground is permitted according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the dispute about washing with water heated before שבת. He says it only applies to water kept in a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water in a כלי looks like it may have been heated on שבת itself, so people might come to permit water heated on שבת. Water sitting in the ground does not cause that confusion. So רב חסדא holds everyone permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ground (water collected in a pit or pool in the earth)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is about water in a vessel,
phrases.notes: The dispute about washing with water heated before שבת.

phrases.english: but in the ground, everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute just identified around רבי שמעון's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute applies only to water in a כלי. Water in the ground is permitted by all.

steps.title: Challenge from the incident of the people of טבריא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The מעשה of the people of טבריה involved water in the ground, and the רבנן still forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the incident of the people of טבריה was with water in the ground, and the רבנן forbade it to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's statement with a known story. In that story, water in the ground was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said water in the ground is permitted by everyone. Yet in the טבריה case, water heated by the ground was forbidden by the רבנן. So it cannot be true that everyone permits water in the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages forbade it to them

steps.confusionAlert: The word וְהָא here does not mean 'and this.' It introduces a challenge: 'But isn't it the case that...!'

phrases.english: But the incident of the people of Tiberias
was with water in the ground,
phrases.notes: Water heated by the natural hot springs in the earth.

phrases.english: and the Sages forbade it to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב חסדא's claim in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that water in the ground is permitted by everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known case shows the רבנן forbidding water in the ground, so not everyone permits it.

steps.title: רב חסדא's statement is flipped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the version of רב חסדא's statement. The dispute is about water in the ground, and water in a כלי is forbidden by everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: The dispute is about water in the ground. But in a vessel, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the challenge by giving the correct version of רב חסדא's words, which is the reverse of the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the טבריה case fits, because the רבנן who forbade it are one side of the dispute about ground water. Water in a כלי, which looks more like water heated on שבת, is forbidden by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)

steps.whyThisMatters: The correct version of רב חסדא's statement is the one in which water in a כלי is forbidden by everyone.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, this is how it was stated:
The dispute is about water in the ground,
but in a vessel, everyone agrees it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 12 by reversing step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction: re-stating the original מימרא in reverse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ground water is permitted by all, and the dispute is about a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ground water is the subject of the dispute, and water in a כלי is forbidden by all.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in this dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement gives the final ruling in the dispute about washing with heated water. The ruling follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was defining what the argument is about. Now it moves to which opinion is the practical הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the dispute to ruling on it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Did you hear this explicitly or by inference?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רבה בר בר חנה whether רבי יוחנן said this ruling openly or whether he only worked it out from a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Did you hear it explicitly, or did you hear it from a general rule?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף checks the source of the ruling. Was it a direct quote, or was it worked out from a general rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling inferred from a general rule is weaker, because the rule may have exceptions. רב יוסף wants to know how solid this ruling is. This question sets up the גמרא's explanation of which general rule is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: From a general rule, by inference

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
Did you hear it explicitly,
or did you hear it by inference from a general rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפֵירוּשׁ שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ, אוֹ מִכְּלָלָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of the ruling given in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן's ruling was stated explicitly or inferred from a general rule.

steps.title: The general rule: the הלכה follows the compromiser
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the general rule רב יוסף had in mind. When two opinions disagree and a third takes a middle position, the הלכה follows the middle position.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the general rule? As רב תנחום said in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי ינאי, in the name of רבי: Anywhere you find two who disagree and one who decides between them, the הלכה follows the one who decides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which general rule רבה בר בר חנה might have used to reach his ruling. This is the rule of the מכריע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה takes a middle position between the other two opinions, so he is the מכריע. If רבי יוחנן only taught this general rule, then רבה בר בר חנה may have applied it here on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: One who decides between them with a middle position

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major rule for deciding הלכה across ש״ס: the compromise opinion usually wins.

phrases.english: What is the general rule?

phrases.aramaic: — דְּאָמַר רַב תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: As Rav Tanchum said that Rabbi Yochanan said
that Rabbi Yannai said that Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: The brackets fix the name: read רבי instead of רב. That's רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Any place that you find
two who disagree and one who decides between them,
the halacha follows the words of the one who decides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the general rule referred to in רב יוסף's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is that the הלכה follows the מכריע when two disagree and a third takes a middle view.

steps.title: The exception: insignificant strips of cloth
steps.stepSummary: The rule has an exception. In the case of קולי מטלניות, רבי עקיבא is the מכריע between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, but the הלכה does not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for the leniencies of small cloth strips. There, even though רבי אליעזר is strict, רבי יהושע is lenient, and רבי עקיבא decides between them, the הלכה does not follow the one who decides.
steps.whatsHappening: The general rule gets an exception. One famous case does not follow the מכריע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the rule of the מכריע is not automatic. That is exactly why רב יוסף asked whether the ruling was explicit, since a rule with exceptions is less certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Small, insignificant strips of cloth (for טומאה purposes)

phrases.english: except for the leniencies of small cloth strips,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַחְמִיר,
phrases.english: where even though Rabbi Eliezer is strict,
and Rabbi Yehoshua is lenient,
and Rabbi Akiva decides between them,
the halacha does not follow the words of the one who decides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted rule with its exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קולי מטלניות the הלכה does not follow the מכריע, רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why the exception: רבי עקיבא was a student
steps.stepSummary: The first reason for the exception is that רבי עקיבא was a student of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. The second reason begins at the end of the amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, because רבי עקיבא is a student. And furthermore, didn't...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why רבי עקיבא's middle position does not win in this case. The second reason starts here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student cannot decide between his own teachers, so the rule of the מכריע does not apply. The words וְעוֹד: הָא open an additional reason that is finished on the next amud.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is that the הלכה follows the מכריע. But a student who takes a middle position between his own teachers does not count as a מכריע.

phrases.english: First, because Rabbi Akiva is a student.
phrases.notes: He was the student of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the exception stated in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The exception of קולי מטלניות to the rule of the מכריע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's status as a student of the two disputants, with a second reason beginning at the end of the amud.
